model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: AFFO per share trajectory and FY2026 guidance: AFFO/share $1.28 (FY2021) -> 1.41 -> 1.50 -> 1.60 -> 1.63 (FY2025) -> $1.65 guided FY2026 (+1.2%). fcf_3yr_cagr is the AFFO/share CAGR FY2022-FY2025 (4.9%); fcf_5yr_cagr is the FOUR-year FY2021-FY2025 AFFO/share CAGR (6.2%) because FY2020 AFFO was not pulled. Selected 3.0% is the base-case steady-state AFFO growth: Same Store NOI guidance 1.15% (revenue 1.9% vs opex 3.5%), plus BTR/fee income and disposition-funded buyback accretion, less the interest drift as 3.9% debt refinances.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-2.5% 3yr) diverges from revenue (6.8%) and EPS (15.1%) by far more than 30%. Book equity is historical-cost real estate net of ~US$730m/yr depreciation, dividends and buybacks, so it shrinks while the business grows; EPS is inflated by gains on home sales (US$218m FY2025). Neither is the growth anchor for a REIT; AFFO per share is.
historical_growth.notes: Decelerating: AFFO/share growth 10.2% (FY22), 6.3% (FY23), 6.7% (FY24), 1.8% (FY25), 1.2% guided (FY26). The FY25-26 slowdown is the transition from acquisition-led growth (now legislatively closed by the July-2026 ROAD to Housing Act for existing homes) to same-store plus BTR/fee growth, plus higher interest on refinanced debt. SBC is ~1% of revenue and stable, so the house/street gap is small (~$0.05/share of AFFO).

scenario_narratives.base: INVH becomes a same-store compounder rather than an acquirer: ~1-2% same-store NOI growth, a modest BTR/fee-income layer, and a disposition-funded buyback that adds ~1%/yr per share, netting to ~3% AFFO growth after the interest drift. AFFO per share reaches ~$2.00 by FY2030. Capitalised at 8.75% with a 16x terminal multiple, the stock is priced about where it should be.
scenario_narratives.bull: The ROAD Act turns out to be a moat rather than a cap: institutional competitors cannot buy existing homes either, INVH's BTR pipeline is exempt, rents re-accelerate to 3%+, and the buyback at a discount to private-market home values continues. AFFO growth of 4-4.5% and a re-rating toward an 18-19x multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Growth is legislated away: acquisition of existing homes is closed, rent restrictions follow the FTC settlement into state law, opex inflation outruns rent, and refinancing 3.9% debt at 5%+ eats the same-store growth. AFFO is flat to +1.5% and capitalised at 9.5% with a 13.6x terminal multiple. Solvency is not the issue (5.4x, IG, 4.4x fixed-charge cover); the issue is a permanently slower compounding rate.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Capitalise AFFO, the post-interest owner flow, at the cost of equity, with net debt held at zero to avoid the REIT double-count. The house basis re-deducts the SBC that Core FFO adds back. The growth path, not the margin, carries every operating judgment: FY2026 follows guidance ($1.65 AFFO/share on a shrinking count = fewer AFFO dollars), then 3% steady state fading to 2.5%. The terminal multiple is a Gordon value (~16x AFFO base), not a re-rating bet.
key_risks_to_valuation: Regulation: the ROAD to Housing Act (July 2026) bans institutional purchase of existing single-family homes; further rent-control or eviction restrictions in Sunbelt states would compress the same-store growth the base case assumes.
Refinancing: US$8.6bn of debt at a 3.9% weighted rate with 4.4 years to maturity rolls at 5%+; every 100bp on the whole stack is ~US$86m, ~9% of AFFO.

Disposition-for-buyback trade: the FY2026 AFFO-dollar decline is deliberate (selling homes above the value implied by the share price). If private-market home values fall, the trade stops being accretive and the growth path is too high.
Opex inflation: guided property tax +4-5% and insurance +5-7% against revenue +1.9%; Same Store NOI guidance is only 1.15%.
Mortgage-rate relief narrowing the ~$1,000/month rent-vs-buy gap would lift turnover and cap rent growth.
Share count: 594.27m is the 30-Jun-2026 count; ~US$100m of Q3 repurchases (~3.7m shares) are not yet in it, a ~0.6% understatement of per-share value.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance v8 chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 24.25-30.89.
data_sources.financials: INVH_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, FY2014-Q2 2026) for revenue, net income, OCF, SBC, debt, cash, shares; Q2 2026 (8-K 2026-07-29, acc 0001687229-26-000041) and Q4 2025 (8-K 2026-02-18, acc 0001687229-26-000013) Earnings Release and Supplemental Information on EDGAR for FFO/Core FFO/AFFO reconciliations, diluted shares+units, debt structure, net debt and FY2026 guidance; Q4 2023 and Q4 2022 releases for FY2021-FY2023 AFFO per share.
data_sources.qualitative: INVH_Analysis.json (2026-09-29): ROAD to Housing Act, FTC settlement, ResiBuilt acquisition, buyback program, guidance commentary.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 total revenues (Dec-25 year, US$m; Q4 2025 earnings release). Revenue is the DRIVER line only; the flow that is valued is AFFO as INVH defines it (Core FFO less Recurring Capital Expenditures), which is post-interest and post-TRS tax. The growth path is applied to revenue with a flat margin stack and is to be read as AFFO-dollar growth on a flat share count. FY2026 reported revenue will grow faster than AFFO (ResiBuilt fee-build construction revenue is pass-through, low-margin), so the reported revenue line is NOT the number to reconcile the projection against; AFFO per share is.
inputs.share_count_basis: Period-end diluted count at 30-Jun-2026 from Supplemental Schedule 2(a): 590,613,522 common shares + 2,196,519 OP units + 1,463,520 shares issuable from unvested equity awards = 594,273,561. OP units are included because AFFO per share is computed on shares + units. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the house flow (charging it and diluting for it would double-count) and because further buybacks are funded by dispositions that also remove AFFO -- the per-share effect of the disposition-for-buyback trade is carried in the growth path, not the count. $400m of repurchase authorisation remained at 30-Jun-2026; the Analysis notes ~$700m bought since Dec-2025, i.e. roughly $100m (~3.7m shares) more in Q3 2026 not yet in this count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow discounted is AFFO, which is already AFTER interest expense (FY2025 interest expense ~US$364m). Deducting the US$8,400.4m net debt the company reports at 30-Jun-2026 (total debt per balance sheet 8,526.7 - retained certificates 55.5 - cash ex-deposits 137.3 + deferred financing costs 44.2 + unamortised discounts 22.4) on top would charge the debt twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md). total_debt and cash below are audit-only. Net debt / TTM Adjusted EBITDAre 5.4x (target 5.5-6.0x), 92.4% fixed or swapped, weighted average rate 3.9%, 4.4 years to maturity, no maturities before June 2027, liquidity US$1,546m, BBB+/Baa2/BBB stable.
inputs.cash_note: Balance-sheet cash and cash equivalents at 30-Jun-2026 (XBRL). The company's net-debt bridge uses US$137.3m 'cash ex security deposits and letters of credit', which includes the unrestricted portion of restricted cash.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 AFFO on the HOUSE basis (US$m): Core FFO 1,176.8 less Recurring Capital Expenditures 173.5 = AFFO 1,003.4 (Q4 2025 release, Schedule 1), less the 27.8 of share-based compensation that Core FFO adds back = 975.5. This is the owner flow the valuation capitalises. NOT the CSV operating cash flow of 1,206.2 (pre recurring capex, pre the non-cash-interest and casualty add-backs) and NOT CSV free_cash_flow (capex is untagged in XBRL for this REIT).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 AFFO as reported, US$1.63 per diluted share+unit (615.6m weighted). Street basis. Statutory net income (589.9 in FY2025) is dominated by depreciation and gains on sale and is not used anywhere in this valuation.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash-flow add-back and Core FFO reconciliation line 'Share-based compensation expense' 27,830 (thousands), Q4 2025 earnings release Schedule 1; XBRL StockBasedComp agrees. Core FFO ADDS SBC BACK, so the house basis re-deducts it. The US$5.8m FY2025 cash paid on net-share settlement of equity awards (equity_award_taxes kpi) is treated as a repurchase of the withheld shares -- already reflected in the flat count -- not as a second SBC charge; sbc_incl_equity_taxes therefore equals sbc.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not deducted: INVH carries US$8.4bn net debt; interest income is immaterial and nets inside the interest expense line that AFFO is already after.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases US$53.2m (Q4 2025: 2.23m shares at $27.43 average). H1 2026 US$547.3m (Q1 17.1m shares at $25.66, Q2 3.48m at $28.75); program total US$600m at $26.30 average by 30-Jun-2026 with US$400m authorisation remaining. Funded by wholly owned dispositions (FY2026 guidance midpoint raised to US$850m) at private-market values above the level implied by the share price.
inputs.dividend: US$0.30 per quarter (US$1.20 annualised, raised from $0.29 in Q1 2026) = 73% of FY2026 guided AFFO of $1.65. FY2025 DPS $1.17.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-28T20:00:02Z (NYSE regular close; Yahoo v8 chart meta; 52-week range 24.25-30.89)
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' field carries the COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because AFFO is a post-interest equity flow. USD build: 10-year UST ~4.2%, beta ~0.9 for a large-cap residential REIT, ERP 5.0% -> ~8.7%, rounded to 8.75% base. Bull 8.25% (rate relief, sector re-rating), bear 9.5% (regulatory discount + refinancing of 3.9% debt at 5%+ as the 4.4-year ladder rolls). A Gordon terminal at 8.75%/2.5% is 16.4x AFFO, roughly where the stock trades today (16.1x FY2026 guided AFFO) and below INVH's 2019-2023 range of ~20-30x.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: INVH is the lessor. Its own office/ground leases are immaterial and expensed inside Core FFO.
inputs.nci_treatment: OP units (2.2m) are included in the diluted share count and AFFO is stated before the OP-unit share of income, so NCI is captured through the count rather than deducted from the flow. Redeemable NCI is immaterial.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine with net debt held at zero (same convention as GPT.AX, GMG.AX, CHC.AX, BXP). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'REIT / property trust'. WHY: INVH is a US single-family rental REIT under historical-cost GAAP; net income is depreciation-and-gains noise, OCF is pre recurring capex, XBRL carries no capex tag, and the balance-sheet debt is already paid for inside AFFO. Engine mapping: ebitda_margin_path = Core FFO / revenue (43.1% FY2025), capex_pct_path = Recurring Capital Expenditures / revenue (6.4%), sbc_pct_path = SBC / revenue (1.0%), D&A, cash tax, lease and working-capital paths all zero, so FCF = AFFO less SBC (house) and the street basis is AFFO as INVH reports it. Growth is applied to revenue with the margin stack flat and is to be read as AFFO-dollar growth on the flat 594.27m count. FY2026 revenue growth of ~+9% on the reported line is NOT what the model projects: it is ResiBuilt pass-through construction revenue; FY2026 AFFO dollars FALL ~1.5% because ~US$850m of home dispositions (funding the buyback) remove NOI while the share count falls. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF); fresh build, no reconciliation block.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 at the bottom of guidance ($1.62) as dispositions run at the top of the range. Then near-flat AFFO: Same Store NOI guidance is already only 1.15% with opex (property tax +4-5%, insurance +5-7%) outrunning revenue; rent-control and eviction-restriction measures riding on the FTC settlement and the ROAD Act's political momentum cap rent growth in the Sunbelt; the 3.9% debt ladder rolls at 5-5.5% (~US$100m more interest over the decade, ~10% of AFFO); BTR yields on cost prove lower than the acquisition model they replace. Growth converges to 1.5%.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5% / 2.0% = 13.6x binds below the 14x cap: a 7.4% AFFO yield, the level a politically constrained, 5.5x-levered landlord would be capitalised at.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 = guidance: AFFO $1.65 midpoint on ~598m weighted diluted shares+units (H1 601.9m, H2 ~594m) = ~US$987m, -1.5% on FY2025's 1,003.4 because ~US$850m of dispositions remove NOI while the count falls; on the flat 594.27m count the model reads $1.66 street / $1.61 house, tying to guidance. FY2027-FY2029 hold 3.0%: Same Store NOI ~1.5-2.5% on a ~US$1.7bn NOI base, ResiBuilt fee-build and third-party management income, continued disposition-for-buyback accretion (homes sold near a ~5.5% cap, stock bought at a ~6.2% AFFO yield), less ~US$15-20m/yr of incremental interest as 3.9% debt rolls at ~5%. Fades to 2.5% = rent growth in line with inflation once the accretion trade and BTR ramp are in the base.
base.margin_rationale: Core FFO / revenue held at the FY2025 actual 43.1% (FY2024 44.2%; H1 2026 40.0% on ResiBuilt pass-through revenue). Flat by construction: the margin stack is held so the growth path alone carries the AFFO story. The interest-cost drift and opex-above-revenue dynamic (guided opex +3.5% vs revenue +1.9%) are in the growth path, not the margin.
base.sbc_rationale: SBC 27.8/2,729.3 = 1.02% of revenue in FY2025, 1.07% FY2024, 1.21% FY2023. Held at 1.0%. Core FFO adds it back; the house basis re-deducts it.
base.capex_rationale: Recurring Capital Expenditures (the Core FFO to AFFO bridge, INVH's own definition: spend to preserve value and functionality) at 6.4% of revenue: FY2025 173.5/2,729.3 = 6.36%, FY2024 170.9/2,618.9 = 6.53%, H1 2026 82.3/1,481.7 = 5.6%. Acquisition, BTR development and value-add renovation capex are growth capital funded by dispositions and the balance sheet within the 5.5-6.0x leverage target; they are what the growth path pays for and are not deducted again.
base.tax_rationale: Zero: INVH is a REIT distributing >90% of taxable income; cash income taxes were US$0.08m in FY2025 (TRS only) and are already inside AFFO.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.75% / 2.5% = 16.4x terminal AFFO (6.1% AFFO yield) binds below the 18x cap. The stock trades at 16.1x FY2026 guided AFFO today; 2019-2023 range was ~20-30x.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2026 at the top of guidance ($1.68) with dispositions slower than the raised midpoint. Then 4-4.5%: the ROAD Act restricts institutional purchases of EXISTING homes, so competing supply of professionally managed rentals slows while INVH's BTR pipeline (ResiBuilt, Lennar-style partnerships) is exempt; rent-vs-buy gap of ~$1,000/month persists; SS NOI back to 3%+; buyback accretion continues at the $400m remaining authorisation and beyond. Fades to 3.0%.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.25% / 2.75% = 18.7x binds below the 20x cap; still below INVH's own 2019-2023 average AFFO multiple.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default. Bear lifted to 25% because the July-2026 ROAD to Housing Act has already removed the acquisition-led growth model, the FTC settlement signals more renter-protection rules are politically live, and AFFO/share growth has decelerated from 10% to ~1-2% in four years. Bull held at 25% rather than cut further because the same law also restricts INVH's institutional competitors, the balance sheet is investment-grade with no maturities before mid-2027, and the buyback below private-market home values is a live, funded lever. Same weighting as GPT.AX and CHC.AX on this route.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
